risks: Cost fidelity is a page-count problem: PostgreSQL choices depend on relpages/reltuples from the heap file; Gres has no pages. Synthesising relpages from tuple width reproduces freshly loaded tables but not tables after UPDATE/DELETE (dead tuples keep pages until VACUUM), HOT chains, TOAST, fillfactor. Mitigation: port estimate_rel_size exactly and keep a heap-page simulator per table; measure per file. Most regress plans are steered by enable_* (569 toggles in 51 files) which limits the blast radius.

Statistics fidelity: compute_scalar_stats (MCV/histogram/ndistinct/correlation; deterministic for <=30k rows since all rows are read), estimate_num_groups, eqjoinsel MCV matching, extended statistics (143 errors 'extended planner statistics objects are not supported' in stats_ext) — a large port; any deviation flips plans in stats_ext, join, aggregates.

Unordered output order beyond nested loops: hash join emits probe-side order with LIFO bucket chains; HashAggregate emits simplehash iteration order (depends on hash_any/type hash functions and table growth); UNION dedup likewise. Reproducing needs PostgreSQL's hash functions and simplehash growth policy — feasible but a distinct L item; without it ~1-2k 'same rows different order' lines stay red even with a perfect planner.
Sort tie order: PostgreSQL pg_qsort (median-of-3, insertion sort n<7, presorted check) vs Rust stable sort (window 818 reorder lines); port sort_template.h's algorithm as the Sort node's loop (M).

exec.rs (39k lines) is the serialisation bottleneck for parallel agents: only lane A (Query IR + exec skeleton) may edit it; every other lane creates files under plan/ or edits pgkv/pgcatalog/parser; freeze the Plan/PlanState enum and Executor trait in one small header commit first.

RLS/privilege regressions: RawScan / UnrestrictedTable / ReadPermit are the strongest invariants; the planner must keep them as the sole constructors of scan leaves and pushdown paths; any bypass is a security hole visible in rowsecurity (2,215 lines).

Distributed regressions: sharded pushdowns and try_distributed_inner_equi_join have their own conformance/sharded gates; keep them as paths the planner always prefers for sharded relations until costs exist; index paths must stay local-only (IndexPlacement::Local, non-sharded).

Memory policy: replacing the per-operator 53200 (which today uses the hard-coded 16 MiB constant in sort/DISTINCT/agg/CTE/setops/SRF sites, exec.rs:24253/24427, agg.rs:2872, grouping.rs:496, cte.rs:492, setops.rs:353, srf.rs:2321) with a work_mem GUC + statement-level cap changes behaviour the soak/loadtest harness observes; keep the RangeScanner scan cap.

ANALYZE-time drift: no autovacuum in Gres, so plans over never-analysed tables must use PostgreSQL's un-analysed defaults (which is what the expected files also reflect for tables the tests never ANALYZE) — an advantage only if ANALYZE semantics and defaults match exactly.

Ordered-index encoding for text under non-C collations (en_US in some tests) requires collation sort keys; start with C/POSIX and default collation and accept red where the corpus depends on locale order.

Cursor/portal semantics: cursor.rs assumes materialised results; SCROLL/backward fetch over a streaming plan needs a Materialize under the portal (PostgreSQL does the same) — small but easy to forget.

Phase 0 must land first or the planner cannot be measured on explain/memoize/incremental_sort/select_parallel/merge/partition_prune: their EXPLAIN calls go through PL/pgSQL SETOF text wrappers refused by routine.rs:2112; unblocked statements will then fail longer on plan text.
Parallel-plan accounting is a deliberate fiction (serial execution, nloops multiplied); document it in PG_COMPAT_MATRIX and keep the switch to real workers open.
brief_corrections: The brief says the read path 'does not consult secondary indexes for ordinary scans'. Nearly right; precisely: exec.rs:18151 try_scan_with_local_index consults a single-column LOCAL btree for `col = const` (choose_local_index_equality 18221) and a GIN for `tsvector @@ const` (choose_local_gin_index 18204), only when the relation is not sharded, has no partial aggregate pushed and is an UnrestrictedTable (no RLS). Never for ranges, ORDER BY, joins, multi-column keys. Btree entries are stored under a non-order-preserving key (crates/pgkv/src/key.rs:232-257: u32 length + rowenc::encode_row), so the index is physically equality-only.

EXPLAIN ANALYZE indeed runs the statement for real (session.rs:5196 run_one) but prints `actual rows` only on the ROOT node and 0 on every inner node, `loops=1` everywhere, no timing, no Planning/Execution Time lines (explain.rs:888-896).
read_gate.rs is not an executor operator: it is the linearizable-read `Linearizer` seam (LocalLinearizer no-op / RaftLinearizer ReadIndex), unrelated to planning.
plan_dist.rs's `Gather` (JoinStrategy::Gather) is a distributed strategy (gather rows from ranges), not PostgreSQL's Gather node; there is no parallel-execution concept in pgexec.

--pgexec-blocking-query-memory=20MiB reaches only base scans (collect_cursor_bounded) and joins (JoinPolicy.memory); sorts, DISTINCT, aggregates, grouping sets, CTEs, set operations and SRF buffers use the compile-time constant scanner::BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY = 16 MiB (scanner.rs:939), so the flag does not raise those budgets.

The 'EXPLAIN' files explain, memoize, incremental_sort and the explain_* wrapper calls in select_parallel/merge/partition_prune/partition_join/misc_functions/stats_ext fail on a NON-planner defect: routine.rs:2112 validate_plpgsql_scalar refuses a user-defined SETOF function in the select list ('set-returning function … is only supported in FROM position', 81 statements). Attribute those cascades to that root; the plan text underneath then needs the planner.

The classifier line counts differ: PG_COMPAT_MATRIX.md:37 says 15,520 EXPLAIN lines, scratchpad/classify.py says 27,138 (it also counts rulers/row-count frames inside plan hunks). Both are cited in the report; the planner-only estimate is 24k-27k EXPLAIN lines plus >=3,032 pure-reorder lines (a lower bound measured per hunk) whose cause is plan shape.

exec.rs `Statement::Query` execution is not one function: run_select_traced spawns a spawn_blocking worker and drives PL/pgSQL scalar-function requests from the async side (session.rs:8023 drive_scalar_worker); a plan executor must keep that request channel (routine::with_scalar_runtime) available inside node bodies.
distributed_impact: Leaf scans go through the RangeScanner trait (scanner.rs:716: scan(ScanRequest), scan_cursor (paged, back-pressured), join(JoinRangeRequest), join_strategy[_for_keys]); crates/gres-ranges/src/forward.rs:3260 implements it across ranges; TimestampedRangeScanner (scanner.rs:1146) stamps the statement read timestamp onto sharded requests. The pushdown contract is plan_dist::DistributedScanPlan (plan_dist.rs:336): PredicatePushdown::Conjunctive(ColumnPredicate{column,op,value}), ProjectionPushdown, PartialAggregateSpec, TopKSpec, TextSearchPredicate; plan_dist::plan_join (278) picks Broadcast|CoPartitioned|Gather from Stats::estimated_bytes (StoredRowStats reads the rowid counter and a bounded key count) — a distributed strategy for two SHARDED base tables only, chosen in exec.rs:17885 try_distributed_inner_equi_join. Constraints on a plan tree: (1) every leaf that reads a stored relation must be expressible as a ScanRequest (pushdowns are optional accelerators; residual qual re-applied above); (2) Index Scan / Bitmap / Tid leaves are local-only (try_scan_with_local_index already declines table.sharded; IndexPlacement::Global needs the timestamp-transaction path) so the planner must generate index paths only for non-sharded relations with Local indexes at first; (3) sharded reads carry the statement read_ts, so the plan carries no per-node snapshot state; (4) try_distributed_inner_equi_join becomes one physical join path (DistributedHashJoin) for two sharded base tables with a single equality key, RLS-open, no virtual generated columns, printable as Hash Join with a Gres-specific 'Distributed:' line — the regress corpus has no sharded tables so fidelity is unaffected; (5) RLS/privilege proofs (UnrestrictedTable, ReadPermit) gate the pushdowns (rls::sanitize_scan_plan at exec.rs:17272) and must ride on the leaf Path, not be re-derived; (6) the per-scan memory cap in collect_cursor_bounded is distributed backpressure and should stay. Nothing in plan_dist conflicts with a PostgreSQL-shaped planner: keep it as plan/dist.rs (path generation for sharded relations) and always prefer its paths for sharded tables until they are costed.
explain_today: explain.rs (1,440 lines) is a purely syntactic walk of the parser AST: plan_statement (77) -> plan_query (121) -> plan_set_expr (137) -> plan_select (162) -> plan_from (225) / plan_table_expr (268) / scan_node (298). It prints Seq Scan on <rel> [alias] + Filter (single relation prints unqualified columns), Nested Loop for every join with Join Filter, Subquery Scan, Function Scan for anything else, HashAggregate + Group Key for GROUP BY and DISTINCT, Aggregate for plain aggregates, Unique + Group Key for DISTINCT ON, Sort + Sort Key (with set_dummy_tlist_references parentheses rule at 344), Limit, Result + One-Time Filter, Values Scan on \"*VALUES*\", Append (+HashAggregate for UNION), Insert/Update/Delete on <rel>. Never Hash/Hash Join/Merge Join/Materialize/Memoize/Index*/Bitmap*/Gather/Incremental Sort/GroupAggregate/MixedAggregate/SetOp/WindowAgg/ProjectSet/CTE Scan/LockRows/Recursive Union. session.rs:5176 explain: describe_statement first (so 42P01/42703 match), if ANALYZE runs the statement via run_one and takes rows.len(), then renders. render_text_node (871): fixed ' (cost=0.00..0.00 rows=0 width=0)' when COSTS on, ' (actual rows=N.00 loops=1)' with N only on the root, no timing, no Planning/Execution Time, no Rows Removed, no VERBOSE Output/schema qualification; render_json/yaml/xml (907/972/1000) emit Node Type, Parallel Aware, Async Capable, Relation Name, Alias, Disabled and the detail keys only (no cost/rows/width/actual/Planning/Triggers). The deparser (deparse_with/deparse_bare_with 494/605, cast_operand, subscript_base, field_base, deparse_plain_call, plan_sort_key, sort_order_suffix, binary_op_text via eval::op_spelling) is a real ruleutils port worth keeping; known gap: untyped constants print '-3' not '-3'::integer because the AST carries no types (676). parser.rs:6095 accepts but discards buffers/wal/timing/summary/settings/generic_plan/memory/serialize; ExplainOptions (ast.rs:1805) holds only analyze/verbose/costs/format. The corpus's explain_filter/explain_mask_costs/... wrappers are user SRFs in the select list, refused by routine.rs:2112, so those tests never reach the renderer.
index_read_path: Reads consult a secondary index only in exec.rs:18151 try_scan_with_local_index (called from scan_stored_relation 17274 when the relation is not sharded, no partial aggregate is pushed, and rls::UnrestrictedTable::from_decision proves no RLS): (a) tsvector @@ const via choose_local_gin_index (18204) + lookup_local_gin (11533) + gin_candidate_rowids (11555, BTreeSet<u64> rowid sets with And/Or folding, prefix terms and NOT bail out); (b) col = const via choose_local_index_equality (18221: first single-column Local btree matching a PredicatePushdown::Conjunctive Eq predicate) + lookup_local_index_equal (11509: scan_prefix over secondary_index_entry_prefix, collect rowids, visible_rows_for_rowids 11601 reads each version chain under the snapshot, recheck indexed values). Everything else is a full scan (RangeScanner::scan_cursor over rowid intervals). What physically stores entries — index_entries (exec.rs:11240): IndexMethod::Btree -> one entry of the key tuple; Gin -> one entry per tsvector lexeme (only tsvector; jsonb/array GIN not indexed); Hash/Gist/Spgist -> NO entries (catalog-only); any expression key -> no entries; brin refused at CREATE ('index access method \"brin\" is not supported', 36 errors); expression indexes catalog-only and restricted (17 errors); partial indexes refused (42 errors); INCLUDE refused (27 errors). The catalog Index (crates/pgcatalog/src/lib.rs:397) has no per-column direction/nulls/opclass/collation, no predicate, no include list. Key layout crates/pgkv/src/key.rs:232-257: [table_id][index_id+INDEX_PRIMARY][u32 len][rowenc::encode_row(canonicalize_row_for_key(values))][rowid]; rowenc.rs:1 'It is NOT order-preserving'; keyenc.rs:1 'Sortable encodings for arbitrary PRIMARY KEY column types are deferred'. So indexes are NOT ordered: no range probe, no leading-column prefix, no ORDER BY satisfaction, no Merge Join input, no Index Scan Backward. Entries carry no xmin/xmax, so every index read is a bitmap-heap-scan-with-recheck; there is no visibility map, so Index Only Scan (Heap Fetches: 0) is not honestly available. Unique constraints and FK lookups use the same equality probe on the write path (local_index_entry_ops 11220, backfill 10060). What an Index Scan / Index Only Scan / Bitmap Heap Scan need: (1) pgkv keyenc.rs memcomparable encoding for indexable Datums (ints, numeric, text under C collation, date/time, uuid, bool, arrays for GIN keys) with NULLS FIRST/LAST and DESC by inversion, drop the length prefix, add secondary_index_range(start,end); rebuild by re-running local_index_backfill_ops (greenfield, no migration); (2) pgcatalog Index/NewIndex per-key (expr|column, direction, nulls_first, opclass, collation), predicate, include; pg_index indkey/indoption/indexprs/indpred rows; (3) pgexec IndexPath builder (indxpath.c port using existing builtin_opclasses.rs/builtin_opfamilies.rs), an ordered index cursor in scanner.rs (local KV only; IndexPlacement::Global excluded until global-index reads exist), a bitmap path over rowid sets (already the shape of gin_candidate_rowids + visible_rows_for_rowids), Index Cond vs Filter split, Recheck Cond; (4) hash-method entries are a one-line change in index_entries; GiST/SP-GiST/BRIN operator scans are a separate XXL. Merge Join, ORDER BY via index, Merge Append and Index Scan Backward all follow from (1)+(3).
memory_policy: --pgexec-blocking-query-memory (crates/gres/src/lib.rs:857; CI passes 20MiB from scripts/gres-pg-regress.sh:267) -> SqlEngine.blocking_query_memory (pgexec lib.rs:409) -> Session -> SubCtx.blocking_query_memory (subquery.rs:44) -> JoinPolicy.memory (subquery.rs:171). It is a PER-OPERATOR cap on retained bytes that raises 53200 'blocking query exceeded the memory budget' (scanner.rs:1136) instead of spilling: applied by collect_cursor_bounded (each base scan, scanner.rs:951), push_bounded_join_row / JoinIndex::build / count_join_rows (join.rs), the lateral cache (exec.rs:13818), key_source_rows (each sort, exec.rs:24251), ensure_blocking_rows_fit (DISTINCT, 24423), agg.rs:2872 (groups), grouping.rs:496, cte.rs:492, setops.rs:353, srf.rs:2321. Inconsistency: the sort/DISTINCT/aggregate/grouping/CTE/setops/SRF sites use the compile-time constant scanner::BLOCKING_QUERY_MEMORY = 16 MiB (scanner.rs:939), not the configured 20MiB; only scans and joins honour the flag. Corpus effect: 104 statements fail with 53200 (type_sanity 23, opr_sanity 18 — catalog self-joins pg_proc x pg_type —, tuplesort 16, join 10, portals 5, limit 4, psql 3, numeric 3, memoize 3, brin* 7, …). PostgreSQL's work_mem (4MB default; regress sets 64kB in tuplesort/incremental_sort/memoize/join_hash/select_parallel) is a SPILL threshold that only changes Sort Method / Batches / lossy-bitmap text, never the answer; Gres answers 'unrecognized configuration parameter \"work_mem\"' (4 errors). Planner interaction: work_mem is an input to cost_sort, cost_agg's hash-vs-sort choice (hash_mem_multiplier x work_mem), ExecChooseHashTableSize batches (printed by join_hash), Memoize cache size, bitmap lossiness, Materialize decisions. Recommendation: (a) add a work_mem GUC that feeds the cost model and the ANALYZE text (Sort Method: quicksort/top-N heapsort/external merge, Batches: n, Memory Usage masked by tests); (b) make the flag a STATEMENT-level hard cap on total retained bytes (still 53200 when exceeded) rather than per operator, and raise it for the regress run so opr_sanity/type_sanity fit; (c) keep the RangeScanner scan cap unchanged (distributed backpressure); (d) real spill-to-disk sort and hash-join batching is a later optional operator feature — a planner-chosen hash join or sort must never turn a query that PostgreSQL answers into a 53200.
